item.title: Costco food court item packs more protein than anything else on the menu, but there's a catch
item.description: A registered dietitian weighs in on Costco's highest-protein food court item, noting its 840 calories and sodium content may surprise shoppers.
item.content:encoded:
One of Costco's newer food court additions is packing more protein than anything else on the menu, but a dietitian says shoppers should look beyond the eye-catching number.

The Rotisserie Chicken Chef Salad, which Costco highlighted among its new food court offerings this year, contains 59 grams of protein along with 840 calories.

The $7.99 salad includes rotisserie chicken, hard-boiled eggs, bacon bits and shredded cheddar cheese on a bed of romaine lettuce, along with tomatoes and creamy peppercorn ranch dressing.

COSTCO BRINGS BACK A FAN-FAVORITE FOOD COURT TREAT AFTER YEARS OFF THE MENU

Jamie Lee McIntyre, a Florida-based registered dietitian nutritionist, told Fox News Digital that protein is only one factor consumers should consider when deciding what to eat.

"That's just a nutrition attribute," McIntyre said of protein. She noted that "a food can be high in protein, but it can also still be high in sodium, saturated fat or calories."

Regarding this particular Costco menu item, McIntyre said the protein "is coming from some good whole foods, chicken and eggs. There's veggies in there. So those are some good building blocks of the meal. But I would say, for a lot of people, 840 calories might be a bit much for a light lunch."

COSTCO SHOPPERS CHALLENGE INFLUENCER'S CLAIM THAT 'INSANE' CHICKEN MEAL CAN FEED FAMILY OF FIVE

Other Costco food court options aren't far behind the chef salad when it comes to protein.

The Chicken Caesar Salad contains 58 grams of protein, just one gram less than the Rotisserie Chicken Chef Salad.

The Chicken Bake is another high-protein option, with 53 grams.

Online reactions to the Rotisserie Chicken Chef Salad have been mixed, with some Costco shoppers criticizing its proportions and others praising its flavor.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Tons of toppings, not enough lettuce. Salty for a salad. I wouldn't buy it again, the portions are just way off, and it was a whole thing to assemble," one Reddit user said.

Another Reddit user was a fan of the salad, particularly the dressing.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Someone bought me one, and I went back 2 days later to buy another," someone wrote. "I am not a salad person, but I love this dressing. I wish I knew what company makes the Peppercorn Ranch dressing."

Fox News Digital reached out to Costco for comment.

item.title: Missouri mom who put newborn in oven instead of crib learns fate as murder charge dropped
item.description: Mariah Thomas told Kansas City police she mistook the oven for a crib. The infant was found with severe burns across her body in February 2024.
item.content:encoded:
A Missouri mother who said she accidentally put her 1-month-old baby in an oven instead of a crib will spend more than a decade behind bars after reaching a deal that wiped away a first-degree murder charge.

Mariah Thomas, 28, pleaded guilty Tuesday to first-degree endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death and was ordered to serve 13 years in the Missouri Department of Corrections, according to Jackson County court records.

The punishment came more than two years after Kansas City police found Thomas' infant daughter dead with severe burns inside a city home.

NEW MEXICO WOMAN'S BODYCAM CONFESSION ABOUT HIDING NEWBORN BABY IN HOSPITAL GARBAGE TOSSED BY STATE COURT

Thomas was also charged with first-degree murder, but that count was dismissed as part of the plea agreement, court records show. She received no probation and will be credited for time already served.

The nightmare unfolded on Feb. 9, 2024, after officers were called to the home around 1:30 p.m. on charges involving a report of a baby who was not breathing, according to charging documents.

Police arrived to find the 1-month-old child with apparent burns across her body. Kansas City Fire Department personnel pronounced her dead at the scene.

Investigators were told Thomas had gone to put her daughter down for a nap but "accidentally placed her in the oven instead of the crib," the documents state.

FLORIDA 3-YEAR-OLD DIES AFTER TRAGIC INCIDENT INVOLVING COMMON PLAY TOY AT BABYSITTER'S HOUSE

A family member later told detectives that Thomas said, "I thought I put [her] in her crib and I accidentally put her in the oven."

The child was wearing a bodysuit over a diaper, and investigators said her clothing appeared to have melted onto the diaper. Police also recovered a baby blanket with significant burn marks from the living room, according to the probable cause statement.

The infant was identified by FOX 4 Kansas City as Za'riah Thomas.

Thomas initially declined to speak with detectives after being advised of her rights, but she agreed to provide a blood sample and allow investigators to access data from her cellphone, the documents state.

STARVING TODDLER ATE DIAPERS AND DRYWALL BEFORE DYING IN FILTHY ROOM WHILE PARENTS LIVED CLEAN, POLICE SAY

Then-Jackson County Prosecutor Jean Peters Baker called the child's death a "gruesome" tragedy when the original charge was announced in February 2024.

"We acknowledge the gruesome nature of this tragedy, and our hearts are weighted by the loss of this precious life," Baker said at the time. "We trust the criminal justice system to respond appropriately to these awful circumstances."

The original complaint charged Thomas only with first-degree endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death.

Court records show prosecutors later added the first-degree murder count that was ultimately dismissed under Tuesday's agreement.

NORTH DAKOTA MOM STABS HER 2 CHILDREN TO DEATH IN 'HORRIFIC' KILLING THAT LEFT COPS TRAUMATIZED: OFFICIALS

Judge Sarah A. Castle found Thomas entered the guilty plea freely and voluntarily and understood the charge and consequences. The judgment states Thomas had no mental disease or defect defense.

Thomas was returned to the Jackson County sheriff’s custody to await transfer to state prison. The judge also ordered her to pay $68 to Missouri’s Crime Victims’ Compensation Fund and waived all other court costs.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Jackson County prosecutor's office for comment.

item.title: Bodycam footage captures moments after ICE shooting of Venezuelan migrant in Austin
item.description: Austin Police Department body camera footage captures the moments after an ICE officer shot a Venezuelan migrant during an arrest attempt.
item.content:encoded:
The Austin Police Department on Tuesday released body camera footage showing the arrest of an illegal Venezuelan immigrant who was shot moments earlier by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers over the weekend.

Three short videos detail the local police response to the shooting of 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garces Perez on Sunday as ICE officers attempted to take him into custody.

In one video, what sounds like three gunshots can be heard. Another clip shows an officer arriving at the scene, where Garces Perez is seen sitting hunched over in the driver's seat of his vehicle and appearing to grab his left shoulder in pain.

DEM REACTIONS WITHIN MOMENTS OF AUSTIN ICE SHOOTING SPARK VIRAL OUTRAGE LOCALLY, ONLINE: 'DISQUALIFYING'

Officers wearing body cameras assisted Garces Perez out of the vehicle, contradicting claims that he was pulled out by agents, before placing him under arrest.

Another officer is heard ordering someone to get a pair of shears to cut open Garces Perez's shirt to examine his wounds.

ICE RESUMES NATIONWIDE TRAFFIC STOPS UNDER NEW POLICY REQUIRING BODY CAMERAS

"¿Tiene armas?" an officer asks in Spanish, inquiring if Garces Perez has any firearms.

"No," Garces Perez replies.

"He's got… looks like one gunshot wound so far," an officer is heard saying.

Garces Perez was reportedly delivering a DoorDash order when he made a U-turn under a highway before ICE agents continued to pursue him. His attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, claimed an unmarked truck chased her client and sideswiped his vehicle before he was shot.

SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN

Authorities confirmed Garces Perez had a final order of removal. However, Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client received the order after a hearing notice was sent to his previous address, despite him having updated his address with the court.

ICE has disputed rumors surrounding the shooting and Garces Perez's legal status, noting that his work permit expired in 2025 and that holding one does not confer legal status in the United States.

The agency also stated that Garces Perez was released from the hospital and arrived at an ICE detention facility just hours later, where he slept on a bed. ICE rebuffed allegations that Garces Perez was indiscriminately targeted.

"This illegal alien was the subject of a targeted vehicle stop," ICE said in a statement. "What makes someone a target for immigration enforcement is whether or not they are illegally in the U.S. Resisting officers and evading arrest is dangerous for our officers, illegal aliens, and the public. We remind the public that resisting officers and evading arrest is a felony and a federal crime. Sanctuary politicians need to stop encouraging this dangerous behavior that puts our officers and the public at risk."

item.title: Florida woman reaches plea deal after months behind bars for allegedly having drugs fall out of 'jail purse'
item.description: Reagan Cox struck a plea deal on charges of introducing contraband into a Brevard County jail after cocaine allegedly fell from her "jail purse."
item.content:encoded:
A plea deal has been struck between prosecutors and a Florida woman who allegedly had drugs placed in her "jail purse" by someone during an intimate encounter. That was her story anyway.

Reagan Cox was arrested in late June on charges of resisting an officer without violence during a traffic stop. At the time, the Brevard County Sheriff's Office's social media announcement didn’t mention the reason for the stop.

Sheriff Wayne Ivey, I assume, was more concerned with telling the story of how the 30-year-old had introduced contraband into a jail using her butt. Understandable, but we have those details now.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

We now know that officers said she was "failing to maintain a single lane of travel" prior to being pulled over. They claimed she was "slow" and "lethargic" and that they smelled "the odor of burnt marijuana."

Cox was in court Tuesday and The Smoking Gun reports that she entered pleas to the charges of introducing contraband into a jail and obstruction. Prosecutors dropped a drug possession count.

TENNESSEE WOMAN ACCUSED OF TURNING TRAFFIC STOP INTO A SHOW FOR PASSING DRIVERS BY ALLEGEDLY EXPOSING HERSELF

She was reportedly placed on 18 months of probation and fined about $700 by a Circuit Court judge. In addition to that, she was sentenced to 70 days in jail, which she had already served following her arrest.

Some may say it was a summer lost for her, but considering how the abnormality in her lower region turned into a baggie of what tested positive for cocaine at her feet after falling out of her jail purse, it could have been worse.

We may never get to the bottom of how the substance, whatever it was, ended up in her possession. But we are getting an end of sorts to this chapter of the story.

The true test of whether anything was learned during this summer behind bars will come now that a plea deal was reached. One can hope that the jail purse, as was so eloquently described by the sheriff, is no longer put to use.

That would be a win for all.

item.title: Bears may have to turn to 3rd-string quarterback as Tyson Bagent falls into concussion protocol: report
item.description: Tyson Bagent is in the NFL's concussion protocol, casting major doubt on the Chicago Bears' backup plan with Caleb Williams also week-to-week.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears got much better news than expected with Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury, but the franchise quarterback is still going to miss playing time.

Bears fans, though, might not be seeing the usual backup, Tyson Bagent, in Week 3.

Bagent is in the NFL’s concussion protocol, according to NFL Network, leaving doubts about his availability on "Monday Night Football" against the Philadelphia Eagles.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Williams also wasn’t entirely ruled out by head coach Ben Johnson, but in the likelihood he won’t be available, mixed with Bagent potentially not clearing protocol in time, the Bears would be forced to go to their third-string quarterback.

That’s veteran Case Keenum, who would be making his first start in the NFL since 2023 if he is called upon to do so.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Bagent was the one who entered the game for the Bears at the very end of a rainy 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in their home opener following Williams' injury. He was sacked on the final play of the game by Dallas Turner to end a potential game-winning touchdown throw.

Now, it’s unclear when Bagent suffered his concussion, though it could’ve come on the final play when he hit the ground hard on the Turner sack.

Bagent, the undrafted quarterback who proved himself his rookie 2023 season after going 2-2 in starts, has been the team’s backup since Williams was drafted first overall in 2024. He hasn’t had to start a game with Williams playing all 17 the past two years.

Again, Williams hasn’t been ruled out, but Johnson did consider him week-to-week during his initial news conference ahead of the Bears’ primetime matchup against an NFC foe.

"He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here," Johnson told reporters. "We’ll see what that looks like."

Bagent finished Sunday’s loss 5-for-9 passing for 54 yards, but it will be interesting to see how much he’s allowed to prepare as the potential starter this week having to go through the protocol stages.

Keenum has 66 starts in his 80 games played across his career in the league, but he hasn’t seen regular-season NFL action since 2023 while with the Houston Texans. He went 1-1 in two starts that year, while his previous games were with the Cleveland Browns in a 2-0 stint in 2021.

If he plays, the Bears would mark the eighth team Keenum has played for in his NFL career.

item.title: Massachusetts youth hockey player suspended after vicious slashing incident goes viral
item.description: Viral video shows an 11-year-old delivering a vicious two-handed slash to a rival's head during a South Shore Kings and Bay State Breakers game.
item.content:encoded:
A youth hockey player in Massachusetts has been dealt an indefinite suspension after a brutal slashing incident that was caught on camera and quickly went viral.

This occurred during a game between the South Shore Kings and the Bay State Breakers at a rink in Foxboro.

In the clip, an 11-year-old Breakers player can be seen skating up the ice before delivering a vicious, two-handed slash to the head of a Kings player.

Just brutal. Shades of Marty McSorely slashing Donald Brashear.

The moment quickly went viral on social media, with many calling for the player to get suspended from the league.

YOUTH PITCHER LAUNCHES FASTBALL AT OPPOSING DUGOUT AFTER ALLEGED ORDER FROM COACH: 'ABSOLUTELY BUSH LEAGUE'

Now, that has happened.

"The Breakers player has been suspended indefinitely from practices and games," the team told 7News (via The New York Post). "Massachusetts Hockey is currently investigating the incident and will decide the length of the suspension, as they are the governing body for our sport."

YOUTH FOOTBALL COACHES FIGHTING & ACTING LIKE FOOLS IN PENNSYLVANIA ISN'T THE LEAST BIT SHOCKING

They also reportedly said that the player who delivered the slash wrote a letter of apology to the victim, who is said to be all right after the incident.

It's a hefty punishment, and a deserved one.

Sure, younger players are going to have some poor judgment at times. However, by that, I mean they sometimes throw a puck out in front of their own net or get caught deep in the offensive zone and give up a breakaway.

I'd argue that an 11-year-old is old enough to know that swinging your stick at another player's head like you're trying to cut down a tree is not okay under any circumstances.

Good on the team for doing the right thing, and hopefully the player is taking plenty of time to reflect on his actions.

item.title: Beyond killer robots: China's real AI threat to America is already here, experts warn
item.description: Experts warn Chinese labs are using "knowledge distillation" and free software to undercut U.S. tech dominance, bypass billions in research, and supercharge cognitive warfare.
item.content:encoded:
While Americans brace for a futuristic AI war of killer robots and bioweapons, experts warn ahead of President Xi Jinping's U.S. visit this week that Beijing is already actively undermining America's global supremacy through AI without ever firing a shot.

Experts who spoke with Fox News Digital outlined a stealthy, three-part playbook, which includes extracting the logic of American models, undercutting U.S. developers with free open-source software, and ultimately weaponizing those systems for things like cognitive warfare. They laid out how China bypasses billions of dollars in U.S. research through labs that interrogate cutting-edge American AI and copy its capabilities, while simultaneously flooding the global market with free alternatives.

"I think a ‘race’ is the wrong metaphor for this," Leah Siskind, an AI research fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital. "I think it's kind of like a multi-front war. And in some places, we're winning and some places we're losing."

XI PREPARES CHINA ‘FOR BATTLE’ AS EXPERT WARNS OF GRAVE DANGER FACING US AHEAD OF DC SUMMIT

While top American tech firms have poured billions into building ultra-expensive, proprietary systems, China has focused heavily on distributing free, open-source models across the globe. Siskind warned that because American tech is costly and the U.S. sector has largely neglected open-source investment, many Fortune 500 companies are making the financial choice to run their operations on Chinese models—unwittingly opening the door to potential CCP censorship, hidden backdoors and, ultimately, global dominance.

"How can you compete with something that's free when American tech is very, very expensive?" Siskind said. "How can we ensure that a Chinese open-source model would be truly clean, that it'd be truly free of CCP censorship? We can't be—we just wouldn't know. And that's by design. We wouldn't know what sort of trick backdoors might be implanted and how that could rear its head later on."

Meanwhile, China expert Gordon Chang warned that Beijing is intentionally using these free models to repeat an economic tactic it previously deployed to corner a different industry.

"This is a tactic that China used with solar panels," Chang told Fox News Digital. "Beijing sees that one day it will drive out the American models on cost and availability, and they will then dominate global AI."

CHAD WOLF: CONGRESS HAS A CHANCE TO STOP CHINA FROM TURNING YOUR CAR INTO A CHINESE SPY

But to flood the market with free software, Beijing first needs the underlying technology—and a way to bypass America's massive lead in computing power.

Chang noted that the U.S. possesses a commanding lead in physical infrastructure, boasting over 5,400 data centers compared to China's roughly 450, along with far superior microchips. To work around the staggering hardware and energy costs required to train artificial intelligence from scratch, Siskind warned that Chinese labs are closing the gap through a process known as "knowledge distillation"—a method where a smaller model essentially interrogates a larger, smarter American model to copy its logic.

"They are able to leapfrog the process by kind of stealing this information," Siskind said, pointing to the Chinese model DeepSeek as a prime example. "This is how they were able to release models like DeepSeek in 2025, which was seismic news because they were able to show that they were really competing with cutting-edge American models and had invested a fraction of the resources."

US ADVERSARY TURNS UP THE HEAT ON AMERICA’S AI LEAD WITH AN UNDERESTIMATED EDGE

The threat is not theoretical. Just last week, the Department of Homeland Security issued a joint cybersecurity advisory warning that Chinese companies are conducting "industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns" to extract proprietary capabilities from U.S. frontier models.

Beyond economic undercutting and software theft, the experts also warned Beijing is simultaneously deploying artificial intelligence into physical supply chains and public influence campaigns.

Rather than sci-fi "killer robots," Siskind emphasized that China's immediate physical priority is "embodied AI"—embedding artificial intelligence into real-world infrastructure like factory automation, commercial drones, and autonomous supply chains. Meanwhile, Chang warned that AI-enhanced propaganda poses a direct threat to American decision-making and democratic sovereignty.

"They're very good at cognitive warfare, and they can enhance their capabilities with artificial intelligence," Chang said. "We do not want our elections determined in China. We do not want our critical national security decisions being made in Beijing. And that's not impossible."

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

As President Xi Jinping arrives in the U.S. this week, the experts who spoke to Fox News Digital said the White House must treat these non-cinematic threats with the same urgency as traditional military posturing.

To protect America's remaining edge, Siskind said Washington must tighten chip export loopholes, blacklist foreign labs engaging in deceptive distillation, and incentivize U.S. open-source development—emphasizing that "it is very important that the most advanced systems are developed under democracy and represent democratic values, as opposed to authoritarian values."

CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN

For Chang, the stakes of that technological defense extend far beyond standard economic competition.

"Xi Jinping throughout this century has been pushing the Chinese imperial-era notion of Tianxia, or 'all under heaven'—that China's rulers have a right to rule the world," Chang warned. "That sounds ludicrous to us, but a Chinese regime powered by AI might actually be able to accomplish that. We certainly do not want our decisions being made in the Chinese capital."

Addressing the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, President Donald Trump reiterated Washington's goal of outpacing China, declaring that U.S. government documents will now refer to AI as "superintelligence."

"The United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control the artificial intelligence being spoken of," Trump told world leaders. "Whoever wins superintelligence wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else. And we're going to keep it that way."

item.title: Dr Drew Pinsky reveals red flag in Presley Gerber addiction treatment before model's death
item.description: Presley Gerber's death at a California rehab facility raises urgent questions about ibogaine treatment and why patients shouldn't direct their own care.
item.content:encoded:
When news broke that Presley Gerber, the 27-year-old son of Cindy Crawford, died Sunday at a California rehab facility, it raised questions about how someone with access to extensive treatment resources could still lose his life to addiction.

According to addiction specialist Dr. Drew Pinsky, Gerber’s case highlights the deadly, progressive nature of substance use disorder — and what he says is a dangerous trend in modern treatment: allowing patients to dictate their own care.

"When I listened to [Gerber's] video, what struck me and concerned me was that the patient seemed to be determining some of the care," Pinsky said on his podcast, "Ask Dr. Drew." "That's never good."

PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY

Pinsky discussed Gerber’s self-reported trip to Mexico for an "ibogaine flood," referring to a high-dose treatment involving ibogaine, a psychoactive compound derived from an African shrub that has been studied as a potential treatment for substance use disorders but is not approved by the FDA.

"I've had patients using ibogaine or ayahuasca for decades, and there's nothing magic about it, I assure you," Pinsky warned, noting that almost every patient he’s seen try the alternative drug eventually relapsed on opioids, often suffering personality changes in the process.

Ibogaine remains an unapproved Schedule I substance in the U.S. due to documented risks of fatal heart arrhythmias, according to federal health agencies.

BRAD PITT SAYS HE CAN DRINK IN ‘RESTRAINED MANNER’ AFTER 7 SOBER YEARS, BUT EXPERT RAISES RED FLAG

Pinsky argued that Gerber’s case highlights how patients struggling with severe substance use disorder are often allowed to bypass proven medical protocols in favor of risky alternative therapies.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Addressing public shock that the young model died inside a treatment center, Pinsky emphasized that high-end rehab centers cannot magically halt severe opioid dependence.

"Opioid addiction is progressive and it ends in death," Pinsky said. "Even with good treatment, it has a worse prognosis than most cancers ... If they are not moving toward recovery, they are moving toward demise."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

While official toxicology results from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office are still pending, emergency dispatch logs indicate that 911 was called to Gerber's facility for a suspected overdose and cardiac arrest.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Dr. Nicholas Kardaris, an addiction expert and CEO of the New York Center for Living, noted that the period inside or immediately following rehab is often the most dangerous window a patient faces.

"People are in rehab because they’re struggling with addiction. It doesn’t mean they’re cured," Kardaris told Fox News Digital, pointing out that when patients relapse in treatment, their lowered tolerance can turn their usual dose into a fatal one.

Medical experts maintain that families needing help for loved ones should seek evidence-based treatment from qualified providers, including FDA-approved medications for opioid use disorders, such as buprenorphine, methadone and naltrexone, when appropriate.

item.title: Joy Behar doubles down on argument US will not elect a woman president
item.description: Joy Behar said America will elect almost anyone before a woman president, sparking pushback from her fellow co-hosts on "The View" while discussing potential 2028 candidates.
item.content:encoded:
"The View" co-host Joy Behar doubled down Tuesday on her argument that a woman could not win the presidency.

The co-hosts discussed Democratic Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker and news he has been on a GLP-1 before delving into a debate about identity politics.

"I think this country will vote for an obese, Jewish, Black, homosexual before a woman," Behar said.

Guest host Star Jones agreed and added, "We just had one of the most beautiful, brilliant women run for president. And you see what we got." 

FORMER FIRST LADY JILL BIDEN DOUBTS SHE'LL SEE A WOMAN PRESIDENT IN HER LIFETIME

Jones was referring to former Vice President Kamala Harris, while Behar said former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton was also unsuccessful.

"You don't win on identity alone, and you don't lose on identity alone," co-host Sara Haines pushed back. 

Alyssa Farah Griffin, the lone Republican co-host, predicted there would be a woman president in the next 20 years.

Patrice Onwuka, vice president for economic policy and director of Independent Women's Center for Economic Opportunity, told Fox News Digital, "This warped view is directly the result of elevating identity politics above common sense and connection.

KAMALA HARRIS BACKS MAJOR CHANGES TO THE SUPREME COURT, ELECTORAL COLLEGE AHEAD OF POSSIBLE 2028 CAMPAIGN

"Joy Behar and Star Jones can’t bring themselves to admit that the female candidates they fawned over could not win over the voters," she continued, referencing the four Americans killed in the 2012 Benghazi attacks during Clinton's time as secretary of state and her infamous comment calling Trump supporters "deplorables."

"Kamala Harris was a failed vice president who oversaw a massive influx of tens of millions of people into America illegally and ran on vibes rather than making Americans’ lives better," Onwuka added. "It was not their looks or gender but their policies and personalities that America rejected."

"I think Joy Behar is taking a very complicated election and giving it a very simple explanation," psychotherapist and author Jonathan Alpert told Fox News Digital. 

"Two women lost to Donald Trump. That doesn’t prove Americans won’t elect a woman. It proves those two women lost those two elections. Sexism may have played a role for some voters, but you can’t take millions of votes and diagnose all of them as sexism." 

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

During an episode of "The View" in July, Behar told her co-hosts, "Think of a woman that could win. Tell me one woman."

During another episode of the show that month, Behar rejected Harris as a potential 2028 candidate.

"I love her, she was great, but she didn't win one time. What makes you think she's going to win again?" Behar asked, adding that anyone who thought Harris should run again and could win was not living in reality.

During an interview with The New York Times published Tuesday, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., said she was weighing a presidential run in 2028, adding, "Pretty candidly, I think about my identity.

"I’m not naïve to the fact that we are living under a very regressive administration, and I happen to be a woman, and I, you know, happen to be Latina," she added. "And I think that there’s a lot of conversation about electability, and I don’t kind of shy away from those realities."

The progressive congresswoman said of a possible White House run, "I think about it personally."

item.title: Battle-tested Zelenskyy sounds chilling alarm on where Putin’s war could head next
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns the risk of Russian drone, missile or land attacks against countries bordering Russia is "very high."
item.content:encoded:
UNITED NATIONS - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Tuesday that Russia could launch attacks against other European countries, telling Fox News Digital that the risk of a new offensive is "very high" as Moscow seeks to undermine European unity and weaken support for Ukraine.

Speaking to reporters following his meeting with President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Zelenskyy was asked by Fox News Digital about the possibility that Russia could invade or attack another European country in the near future.

"That's why the risk of offensive by drones, missiles or land operation is very high against other countries who are bordering Russia or Belarus," Zelenskyy said.

US INTEL WARNS RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH LIMITED ATTACK ON NATO ALLY IN EFFORT TO FRAGMENT ORGANIZATION: REPORT

The Ukrainian leader argued that Russian President Vladimir Putin, unable to achieve his military objectives in Ukraine, could seek to create instability elsewhere in Europe to pressure Western governments into reducing their support for Kyiv.

"How to divide unanimity in Europe? ... To attack somebody else. To attack and say, look, I will go further if you will not stop this," Zelenskyy said.

He pointed to drone incursions and disruptions affecting several European countries, arguing that Moscow is already attempting to intimidate European societies and test their response.

Zelenskyy said Putin's inability to secure a decisive victory in Ukraine could push him toward additional confrontations, as he faces pressure to justify the war to the Russian public.

FINNISH FOREIGN MINISTRY OFFICIAL DETAILS HOW RUSSIA'S 'HYBRID WARFARE' RESHAPED BORDER SECURITY

Asked by Fox News Digital what European countries should do in response to the growing threat, Zelenskyy offered a direct answer.

"Respond. Always respond. It's not about the war. If you don't respond, Russians, they will go further," he said.

The warning comes amid heightened concerns about Russian activity in Europe. Zelenskyy's warning comes amid heightened tensions across Europe following a series of Russian drone incursions and warnings from European leaders about the possibility of further attacks.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned on Sept. 14 that peace in Europe was under threat, urging European countries to take the danger seriously. Speaking at an EU-Arctic Summit in Finland, Merz said Russia's presence in the region and its hybrid attacks elsewhere in Europe were increasing, calling for a united response from European countries and NATO.

RUSSIA’S STRIKES NEAR MOLDOVA RAISE ALARM OVER PUTIN’S PLANS FOR EUROPE’S EASTERN FLANK

The German leader's warning followed an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport on Aug. 4, which German authorities publicly attributed to Russia on Sept. 1.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk issued a separate warning on Sept. 17 that Russia was planning drone or missile attacks against NATO countries supporting Ukraine, including Poland, while potentially portraying the incidents as accidental to weaken the alliance's response.

The concerns are not limited to hypothetical threats. On Sept. 8, a drone entered Romanian airspace before returning to Moldova and crashing, according to Romania's Defense Ministry. A week later, Italian fighter jets operating under NATO's air defense mission shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. Italian officials said the drone most likely came from Russia, although Lithuanian authorities were still investigating its origin.

TRUMP SAYS US WILL LET UKRAINE MAKE PATRIOT MISSILES IN MAJOR POLICY SHIFT

Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs also warned in a Sept. 18 interview with The Guardian that European countries and NATO were struggling to keep pace with developments in drone warfare, highlighting gaps in air and missile defenses that could leave European countries vulnerable to Russian attacks.

Zelenskyy's remarks followed talks with Trump in which the Ukrainian leader said he raised the possibility of a mutual halt to attacks on Russian and Ukrainian energy infrastructure, as well as Ukraine's need for additional Patriot air defense missiles ahead of winter.

"We are ready," Zelenskyy said of a potential agreement to halt energy strikes, adding that he was unsure whether Russia was prepared to reciprocate.

Zelenskyy also said Trump had expressed a willingness to help Ukraine obtain additional air defense capabilities, although no concrete commitment on immediate missile deliveries had been made.

The meeting came as Russia and Ukraine intensified aerial attacks, including strikes on energy infrastructure, ahead of the UN General Assembly.

item.title: Former USPS worker indicted after allegedly dumping 300-plus Utah mail-in ballots without delivering one
item.description: Damon Matai Seei allegedly separated over 300 mail-in ballots from other mail at the start of his shift and discarded them within 90 minutes.
item.content:encoded:
A former U.S. Postal Service (USPS) worker in Utah was indicted after allegedly setting aside more than 300 mail-in ballots at the start of his shift and dumping them without delivering a single one, Department of Justice (DOJ) officials said on charges related to the case Tuesday.

Damon Matai Seei, 34, of Payson, Utah, was indicted by a federal grand jury on Sept. 16, on a charge related to the unlawful secretion, destruction and delay of mail. He was arrested Tuesday and made his initial appearance in federal court in Salt Lake City.

Federal prosecutors allege Seei was working as a letter carrier on June 3, when he was entrusted with delivering mail to more than 300 people in Eagle Mountain, Utah, ahead of the state's June 23 primary election.

USPS WOULDN'T DELIVER BALLOTS IN STATES THAT REFUSE TO FORK OVER MAIL-IN VOTER INFO UNDER PROPOSED RULE

The mail included advertisements and hundreds of mail-in ballots that were clearly marked as ballots, according to DOJ officials.

Officials said Seei separated the ballots from other mail shortly after beginning his shift, did not deliver any of them and discarded them within about an hour and a half. Other mail was also discarded, officials said.

Several voters later complained to the Utah County Clerk that they had not received their mail-in ballots, U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak for the District of Utah said Tuesday.

POSTAL SERVICE THRUST INTO MAIL-IN BALLOT FIGHT AS TRUMP ORDER GETS TIED UP IN COURT

Using county databases, the clerk determined that voter participation was unusually low in the area where the complaints originated, according to Holyoak.

It remains unclear whether the affected voters ultimately received replacement ballots or were able to vote. Holyoak said federal officials are continuing to investigate and plan to contact affected voters to determine whether they were able to cast ballots.

Seei has told investigators that he did not have a political motive, according to DOJ officials. The investigation remains ongoing.

SEVEN NONCITIZENS CHARGED IN NORTH TEXAS ELECTION-INTEGRITY INVESTIGATION

"When American voters lawfully cast their vote, they should feel confident that it is counted," said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. "Allegedly throwing away hundreds of ballots is a serious federal crime that undermines the integrity of our elections. Ballot integrity is not a partisan issue."

The case was investigated jointly by the USPS of Inspector General and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI).

Seei's next court appearance is scheduled for Nov. 30.

item.title: Fox News Poll: Voters question whether AI’s promise outweighs its risks
item.description: A Fox News survey finds 71% oppose AI data centers in their area, but 52% favor remote locations, revealing a stark NIMBY divide among voters.
item.content:encoded:
As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly politicized ahead of the midterm elections, the latest Fox News national survey finds voters struggling to reconcile the technology’s promise with the economic and environmental costs of the data centers needed to power it. 

They are especially against allowing centers in their communities while favoring them in remote locations, creating a "Not In My Backyard" dynamic.

A 71% majority opposes building AI data centers in their area, including 46% who strongly oppose them. Both of those numbers are up a touch since earlier this summer. However, the survey reveals a paradox: a 52% majority favors building them in remote locations (44% oppose).

FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS

The central contrast is seen across community types, as about 7 in 10 urban, suburban and rural voters oppose data centers in their backyards. That consensus fades regarding remote facilities. Half of urban voters (50%) and a majority of suburban voters (57%) favor building them there, while 51% of rural voters remain opposed.

Women, White voters, those without a college degree and Democrats are more likely than men, non-White voters, college graduates and Republicans to oppose data centers, whether near their community or elsewhere.

When presented with arguments for and against data centers, reactions are nuanced. By roughly 30 points, voters are less likely to support construction if told data centers could strain local water supplies (by 28 points), raise energy bills (29 points) or grow to an enormous size (29 points).

FOX NEWS POLL: 71% THINK TRUMP ADMINISTRATION LACKS PLAN TO END IRAN WAR

Opposition softens when voters see direct benefits to daily life or national interests. They are more likely to be supportive if told data centers are necessary for online activities such as streaming and banking (9 points), critical infrastructure like transportation and water systems (13 points) or to help maintain a competitive edge over countries like China (18 points).

These reactions to additional information operate against a backdrop of AI pessimism. Majorities of voters are more likely to see AI as bad rather than good for the U.S. economy (54% bad vs. 36% good), mental health (54-34%), society (56-34%), the environment (60-30%) and jobs (63-29%).

The lone exception is day-to-day life, where more voters say AI is a good thing by 4 points (47% good, 43% bad), down from an 11-point spread in November 2025 (50-39%).

Overall, AI technology is viewed more negatively than positively by 23 points (37% favorable vs. 60% unfavorable), widening from an 11-point deficit in April and 9 points in July. The underlying demographic patterns mirror those for data centers. Democrats (67% unfavorable), White voters without a college degree (65%), women (64%) and independents (64%) are the most negative. The most favorable views come from non-White men (49% favorable), voters with graduate degrees (49%) and MAGA Republicans (46%).

AI & The 2026 Midterms

On the generic congressional ballot, the Democratic candidate is ahead of the Republican by 7 points overall. Republicans have a 21-point advantage among voters who support building data centers in their communities, narrowing to 9 points among those allowing construction only in remote areas. Democrats are ahead by at least 19 points among voters who oppose data centers in either location.

Voters who view AI favorably back the Republican candidate in their district by 7 points, while those with unfavorable views back the Democrat by 17 points.

"In this election, the bottom line is that technology is no longer just a tool. It’s a wedge issue," said Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts the Fox News Poll with Democrat Chris Anderson. "As infrastructure demands force AI into the physical world, campaigns that map tech anxiety onto their voter coalitions will shape the midterm narrative."

Voters think Democrats would better handle building AI data centers by a 14-point margin. That lead is especially strong among Black voters (D +51), voters under age 30 (D +35), Hispanic voters (D +29), and independents (D +26). It narrows among White voters (D +5) and rural voters (D +7), while White rural voters are one of the few groups to say Republicans would do better (R +4). Cross-party defections also advantage the Democrats: 15% of Republicans prefer Democrats on data centers, compared with just 4% of Democrats favoring Republicans.

A few more things…

Three-quarters of voters (76%) favor banning AI in kindergarten through eighth grade classrooms, with some of the strongest preference for the ban among moms (81%).

CLICK HERE FOR CROSSTABS AND TOPLINE

Support for banning cellphones in K-12 classrooms is also high: 72% favor the policy and 25% oppose it.

In addition, a majority supports prohibiting police departments from using automated license plate readers, such as Flock Safety cameras (57% favor vs. 39% oppose).

Age creates the biggest divide. Voters under 30 would ban license plate readers by 28 points, while those 65 and over support them by 7 points. Partisans show unusual agreement on banning the cameras, though by different margins: Democrats by 27 points, independents by 23 points and Republicans by 6 points.

Conducted September 11-14, 2026, under the direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News survey includes interviews with a sample of 1,211 registered voters randomly selected from a national voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (96) and cellphones (821) or completed the survey online after receiving a text (294). Results based on the full sample have a margin of sampling error of ±3 percentage points. Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling error, question wording and order can influence results. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics are representative of the registered voter population. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data.

item.title: Simone Biles buys a new Porsche because her old one now carries the unmistakable stench of theft
item.description: Simone Biles revealed on TikTok that three masked men stole her Porsche GTS from her Chicago-area home, and now she's out shopping for a new car.
item.content:encoded:
Simone Biles revealed on social media that she recently did some car shopping after her Porsche was stolen.

It was recovered, but what is she supposed to do? Drive around in a Porsche that had some car thief cruising around in it?

Hell no.

SIMONE BILES QUESTIONS WHETHER $23,000 FOR A RED CARPET GLAM IS 'THE NEW NORM' IN VIRAL TIKTOK

The former Olympic gymnast broke the news to her TikTok followers the way all news is broken on that platform: while applying makeup.

Biles revealed that her ride was lifted from her Chicago-area home.

"I feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole our Porsche. Stole the GTS," she said.

Now, she didn't specify which model Porsche, but the GTS is a high-performance trim and not generally the sort of thing you see soccer moms wheeling into the unnecessarily tight Trader Joe's parking lot.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Respect on that front.

Fortunately, the car owned by her and her husband, Indianapolis Colts safety Jonathan Owens, was recovered.

Unfortunately, there aren't enough pine-scented fresheners in the world to get rid of the stink that comes with having your car stolen.

Also, it shows up on the ol' Carfax report. That’s going to hurt the Porsche’s trade-in value, although people will still line up to buy Biles' once-stolen Porsche.

Now, there's a case to be made that this is a little out of touch. A strong, compelling case.

But I get it.

If three masked fellas broke into my garage and made off with my mint-condish, sensibly rugged 2025 Ford Bronco Sport (hey, I always catch people eye-balling it), I'd have a tough time driving it.

I still would, of course. I can't just go buy a new car because my old one's feng shui is off, but I get it.

This is not the Biles-Owens household's first run-in with thievery. Back in February, while in Milan for the Winter Olympics, Owens posted on X that someone had tried to steal his shopping bag out of his hand.

However, it appears he kept whatever was in the bag and didn't go buy a replacement.

item.title: NBA's Kevin Durant brushes off Enes Kanter Freedom's WNBA trans debate: 'I don't give a f---'
item.description: Kevin Durant brushed off the WNBA gender eligibility debate at Rockets Media Day, pivoting to the league's sneaker deals and revenue growth.
item.content:encoded:
Kevin Durant wants no part of the WNBA’s gender eligibility debate.

During Houston Rockets Media Day on Tuesday, reporters pressed the veteran forward on the ongoing campaign by his former Thunder teammate, Enes Kanter Freedom, and former NBA first-round pick Royce White to keep biological men out of women's sports.

Durant dismissed the campaign entirely, pivoting instead to the WNBA's recent sneaker deals and revenue bumps, not addressing the core issue of biological males entering female leagues.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"All that stuff used to be noise, man. WNBA is flourishing," Durant said.

"Look what these women are doing. Look at the money they've made over the last few years. Look at visibility of their league. They got four or five signature athletes on major brands that represent major brands. These women have brands for themselves, the business women for themselves outside the game.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT BLAMES THE WRONG PEOPLE FOR ‘SOWING DIVISIVENESS’ IN TRANSGENDER DEBATE

"So a lot of that stuff, the politics that they bring into sports nowadays, I understand the message in behind what they're trying to do, but a person like me who just strictly cares for the purity of the sport, I do not give a f*** about none of that. I care about flourishing and pushing the league forward and that's what's happening right now."

Kanter Freedom and White have spent months actively challenging the WNBA’s gender eligibility loopholes.

FORMER NBA PLAYER ROYCE WHITE SAYS HE IS DECLARING FOR NEXT WNBA DRAFT AFTER ENES KANTER ANNOUNCEMENT

The duo highlighted those gaps by announcing plans to "identify as women" and declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft.

Critics and current WNBA players have dismissed the draft declaration as a stunt; Kanter Freedom maintains his singular mission is protecting female athletes. Royce White specifically targeted the WNBA's current collective bargaining agreement, arguing that the text relies on vague language regarding gender identity and fails to mandate that players be biological females explicitly.

ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTED FROM SKY-FEVER GAME AFTER VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD

The ideological clash spilled into Wintrust Arena in August when Kanter Freedom sat court side at a Chicago Sky-Indiana Fever game. The former NBA center engaged in a heated verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud over the issue, resulting in Kanter Freedom’s ejection and a subsequent venue ban, a move backed by players like Los Angeles Sparks forward Cameron Brink.

Kanter Freedom and White want the league to draw a hard line on who belongs on the floor. The policy clash isn't going away, but KD has made his choice: stick to sports.

item.title: Hasan Piker admits he has 'dialed down' his opinions after public and Democratic backlash
item.description: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker told Jon Lovett that he has toned down his rhetoric amid backlash, but his controversial remarks continue to roil Democratic campaigns.
item.content:encoded:
Twitch streamer Hasan Piker admitted on Friday that he has "dialed down" his commentary since facing backlash for taking part in Democratic candidates' campaigns.

Piker discussed the ongoing controversy surrounding his past statements with "Pod Save America" co-host Jon Lovett, particularly after his Axios interview last week in which he described America as "pound for pound" worse than al-Qaeda on terrorism.

The progressive commentator argued that many of his comments are taken "out of context" or taken from a longer statement but added that, more recently, he has begun to think about what he says and tone down his rhetoric.

HASAN PIKER SAYS HE’D ‘ABSOLUTELY’ CAMPAIGN FOR AOC IN 2028 AS EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF

"There’s also the third thing, which is like actual positions that I hold, actual opinions that I have that are unbelievably antagonistic to those in positions of power, that when they hear that, they like lose their minds," Piker said. "They don't know how to deal with it. And when I'm faced with a question like that, I have to in my mind make this calculation of: Should I be honest about what I believe? Should I take a principled stance on something, or should I portray myself as a campaign surrogate and act as though I am running for office?"

He continued, "And I've definitely dialed down. I know it doesn't seem like it. And I've definitely dialed down my commentary with that in mind for sure."

Piker did not clarify what opinions he has softened but suggested that the backlash against him is largely because Republicans "don't really have a good midterm message."

"Just because it's their most successful narrative doesn't mean that it's going to be successful in winning elections for them. And I don't think it will be successful in winning elections for them at all," Piker said.

FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER CALLED OUT BY MS NOW HOSTS IN FIERY EXCHANGE OVER HIM BEING A DRAG FOR DEMOCRATS

He added, "Because look, I've gone all up and down the country. I have fans in many places all around this beautiful country. And you know, there's obviously a lot of Republicans that don't like me and maybe even some liberals that don't like me, but by and large, the idea that a Twitch streamer is supposed to be held to a higher standard than the president is such an insane phenomena that it could only be concocted by a bunch of out-of-touch people in mainstream outlets that think this is a salient narrative that will definitely work because people don't care."

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment.

Piker has garnered nationwide attention after campaigning with Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during the primary election. Since winning the Democratic primary, El-Sayed has attempted to distance himself from Piker, repeatedly referring to him as a "streamer from California" with no relevancy to the race despite their multiple past appearances.

OCASIO-CORTEZ CALLS FOCUS ON HASAN PIKER 'ABSOLUTELY LUDICROUS' AS SOME DEMOCRATS DEMAND DISTANCE

Other Democratic figures have largely come out against Piker as he continued to make controversial comments, such as suggesting that Jewish Americans were bringing violence upon themselves based on their support for Israel.

Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin himself distanced his party from Piker and his "deplorable" comments during an interview with Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"Let me just say that I think it's absolutely disgusting and deplorable the things that Hasan Piker has said," Martin said. "But he does not represent the Democratic Party, and he certainly doesn't represent the viewpoints of almost every one of our candidates and our elected officials."

item.title: CNN staffers accept new reality as Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros Discovery goes full steam ahead
item.description: CNN staffers reveal mixed emotions as Paramount's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery moves forward following the settlement with State Attorneys General.
item.content:encoded:
A new reality is setting in for CNN's rank and file as the network will once again have new ownership following Paramount's merger with its parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD).

"I think people are like, 'Let's just get this done,'" one CNN staffer told Fox News Digital.

Paramount's $111 billion bid to buy WBD overcame its biggest obstacle, which was the antitrust lawsuit spearheaded by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and several other Democratic State AGs. Instead of battling it out in court during the March 2027 trial date, both parties reached a settlement Monday, paving the way for Paramount CEO David Ellison to take the reins of two legacy Hollywood studios and two major news organizations — CNN and CBS News — among other assets. Negotiated in the settlement is the implementation of an independent editorial board that will oversee both news outlets.

PARAMOUNT REACHES SETTLEMENT WITH STATES SUING TO BLOCK WARNER BROS DISCOVERY MERGER

There have been several reports of internal strife within the CNN newsroom since the settlement was reached, but at least one network staffer believes the sentiment is more nuanced based on conversations they've had with colleagues.

"I think there are fewer people internally opposed to the merger than there used to be," the CNN staffer said. "People internally just want direction."

A second CNN staffer disagreed with the notion that they aren't personally opposed to the merger, telling Fox News Digital, "Nothing has changed about anyone's views at CNN."

"If there is that perception, it is coming from the fact that this has been out there for a long time so people are less loud. That shouldn’t be confused with a change of mindset," they said.

CNN STAFFERS BRACE FOR PARAMOUNT CEO'S POTENTIAL PLAN TO LAUNCH EDITORIAL BOARD TO OVERSEE NETWORK

A lot of unknowns loom over CNN as the merger proceeds. First are the company wide layoffs that are expected to take place that will likely impact CNN. Second is the change in CNN's leadership — whether its current CEO Mark Thompson will remain or whether Ellison's appointed CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss will have a new role overseeing both news operations, as reports previously suggested.

"I don’t know who will run CNN," the second staffer said. "Ellison will have a lot of pressure to make that decision and not to say let Mark Thompson stay on for a little while to not deal with it or fake anybody out. It’s better for his business to make a clean, strong decision and let everybody know."

While they're glad the Paramount merger brings clarity about the network's future, the CNN insider is dreading "fairly dramatic" cuts that will ultimately rock the newsroom.

"CNN will be diminished," the second staffer said. "However, that is already happening macro and micro to us and all other legacy media."

Representatives for CNN and Paramount declined to comment.

FORMER '60 MINUTES' HONCHO SAYS CBS NEWS LEADERS WANTED STAFF TO 'COMPROMISE OUR PRINCIPLES'

Much of the opposition toward the Paramount-WBD merger stemmed from Ellison's taking control over CNN. Liberal critics claimed that as a result of the deal, CNN would be given a MAGA-bent to its coverage, pointing to Ellison and his billionaire father Larry Ellison's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump, and worried Ellison's CNN would be run by CBS News chief Bari Weiss, who has been ostracized by the far-left despite her outspoken left-of-center politics.

Ellison has previously assured that CNN would maintain editorial independence following the merger. In a guest essay published in The New York Times, the Paramount CEO addressed the "speculation" about what would happen to CNN under his ownership.

"I have regularly voted for candidates of both parties; I hold some views that would be called conservative and others that would be called liberal, just like most Americans; and when it comes to our news operations, I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views. I believe that news should be based on facts and truth," Ellison wrote.

"Great news organizations like CNN and CBS News are here to tell it straight down the middle," he added. "That requires newsrooms that reflect the whole world, not one side of it. And it requires independence."

item.title: Biden administration granted woman green card months before she illegally voted in 2024 election: DHS
item.description: Evelyn Miller of the Philippines registered online weeks before Election Day and voted in the 2024 election in Pennsylvania despite not being a U.S. citizen, DOJ says.
item.content:encoded:
A Biden-era noncitizen from the Philippines living in Pennsylvania pleaded guilty to illegally voting in the 2024 election after registering just weeks before Election Day, federal prosecutors said.

Evelyn Miller, 37, of Emmaus, pleaded guilty Sept. 16, to illegally voting in the election.

Miller is a lawful permanent resident but not a U.S. citizen, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania said.

Only U.S. citizens can vote in federal elections.

ICE ARRESTS PERUVIAN NATIONAL ACCUSED OF ILLEGALLY VOTING IN 2024 ELECTION AS DHS CITES SIMILAR CASES

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) began looking into Miller after receiving information that someone living in Lehigh County may have illegally registered to vote or cast a ballot, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said Tuesday.

DHS said Miller registered online on Oct. 9, 2024, less than a month before she voted in person in the Nov. 5 general election.

HSI and FBI agents interviewed Miller at her home in July 2025. Miller told investigators she registered online before the election and then went to her polling place in Emmaus to vote on Election Day, according to DHS.

SEVEN NONCITIZENS CHARGED IN NORTH TEXAS ELECTION-INTEGRITY INVESTIGATION

Miller had received lawful permanent resident status July 19, 2024, during the Biden administration, DHS said.

"This alien from the Philippines pleaded guilty to illegally voting in the 2024 election in Pennsylvania," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said. 

"Thanks to the hard work of the men and women of HSI, as well as our partners at the Department of Justice, this alien will soon face justice for her efforts to subvert our elections. American elections are for Americans only."

HSI investigated the case with the FBI.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ARRESTED IN INDIANA FOR ALLEGEDLY VOTING IN FEDERAL ELECTION: DHS

Miller's case comes as the Justice Department pursues a broader group of election-related cases stemming from the 2024 election.

Federal prosecutors announced Sept. 18 that 16 people had been charged in separate cases involving illegal voting and related election crimes across several states.

Miller is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. 16. She faces up to one year in prison, one year of supervised release and a $100,000 fine, according to federal prosecutors.

item.title: Father of 9/11 hero Todd Beamer appears in Michigan Senate race ad to condemn Hasan Piker rhetoric
item.description: David Beamer, father of Flight 93 hero Todd Beamer, appeared in a campaign ad for Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers condemning Hasan Piker and Abdul El-Sayed.
item.content:encoded:
David Beamer, father of Flight 93 passenger and 9/11 hero Todd Beamer, criticized streamer Hasan Piker and his ties to Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in a campaign video released Monday for El-Sayed's Republican opponent Mike Rogers.

The video, posted by Great Lakes HQ, was produced by the Great Lakes Conservative Fund, a super PAC supporting Rogers. It began with a 2019 clip of Piker saying that America "deserved 9/11" followed by clips of El-Sayed appearing on Piker's Twitch livestream and another of El-Sayed refusing to disavow Piker when prompted.

Beamer, who narrates the ad, then introduced his son Todd Beamer, one of the heroes of United Flight 93 who fought back against the terrorists who hijacked the plane in the terror attacks on September 11, 2001. 

"Those 43 people on Flight 93 were not victims. They were killed in action. When I hear anyone suggest America 'deserves 9/11' my question is, ‘Who would say that?’" Beamer says in the ad.

EL-SAYED TRIES TO PUT THE HASAN PIKER DEBATE BEHIND HIM AS MIDTERMS APPROACH

El-Sayed has repeatedly rejected Piker's 9/11 remark but has resisted calls to completely renounce the streamer, who campaigned with him during the Democratic primary.

Elizabeth Pipko, a former Republican National Committee spokesperson, lamented that families mourning loved ones lost on 9/11 still have to be politically involved to protect their loved ones' legacies.

"How incredibly disappointing that, 25 years after those horrific attacks, Todd Beamer’s family is still unable to simply mourn their son and speak about his heroism. Instead, they find themselves having to teach their fellow Americans a lesson they themselves wish they never had to learn," she told Fox News Digital. 

"Todd Beamer’s family knows better than most the pain that anti-American sentiment and terrorism can inflict on us all. Todd’s character, and the American spirit of grit and guts he embodied, is what we should not only remember, but also look for in the leaders we elect to serve our great country," she added further. "In honor of Todd Beamer and all the brave Americans taken from us too soon, we have a job to do — in November and beyond."

FLIGHT 93 HERO'S DAD WARNS 'ENEMIES FROM WITHIN' AIM TO DESTROY AMERICA AT THE BALLOT BOX

Theo Wold, a former assistant attorney general and former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under Trump, told Fox News Digital that Piker will continue to haunt El-Sayed's campaign as long as the candidate "refuses to denounce" Piker entirely.

"Antifa Democrats and their friends in the media say a lot of dangerous and incendiary things. Hasan Piker, who endorses political violence and has denigrated the Americans killed on September 11th, has repeatedly campaigned alongside his friend El Sayed," Wold said. "El Sayed refuses to denounce Piker not just because they’re friends but Leftists like them don’t believe there are any boundaries when they are pursuing their ideological goals."

EL-SAYED IGNITES FIRESTORM AFTER SHARING 9/11 MESSAGE ON SOCIAL MEDIA: 'PIECE OF S---'

Fox News Digital also reached out to a group representing Gold Star Families, El-Sayed’s campaign, and Mike Rogers’ campaign but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Former news anchor working for California Democrat arrested by immigration authorities at Las Vegas airport
item.description: Ho-Yin Mo, a legislative aide to California Assemblywoman Catherine Stefani, was arrested by federal immigration authorities at Las Vegas airport over an alleged visa overstay.
item.content:encoded:
A staffer for a California Democratic state lawmaker was arrested by federal immigration authorities in Las Vegas, according to reports.

Ho-Yin Mo, who was a news anchor at a Chinese-language news station in San Francisco before becoming a legislative aide to California Assemblywoman Catherine Stefani, was taken into custody Thursday at Harry Reid International Airport.

"On January 13, 2020, Mo lawfully entered the U.S. on a temporary basis but illegally overstayed his welcome by failing to depart by May 15, 2020," the Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital. "Work authorization or a pending application do NOT confer legal status in the United States."

ICE ARRESTS SOUTHWEST AIRLINES FLIGHT ATTENDANT IN NASHVILLE FOR ALLEGEDLY OVERSTAYING VISA SINCE 2021

Mo worked as a field representative for Stefani, who represents portions of San Francisco and San Mateo County. She previously served on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors from 2018 to 2024.

Mo joined Stefani's office in January 2025, according to his LinkedIn profile.

"No one is above the law, not even the California legislature and its staff," First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli wrote on X.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Steafani called for Mo's release.

"Ho Yin is a selfless public servant and a valued, legal employee of the California State Legislature serving our San Francisco and Bay Area communities," she said. "When Ho Yin and I meet our Chinese-American constituents, he brings a unique sense of belonging to so many who watched him as a TV reporter. And his work goes far beyond presence."

"Our whole community eagerly awaits Ho Yin’s return to his home and his job where he is loved and adored," she added.

Mo previously served on former San Francisco Mayor London Breed’s unsuccessful 2024 reelection campaign as an outreach organizer focused on Asian American and Pacific Islander communities, according to the New York Post.

WHITE HOUSE BRINGS RECEIPTS AFTER MEDIA CLAIMS NONCRIMINAL ICE ARRESTS ‘SOARING’: ‘FALSE NARRATIVES’

"When we learned that Mo was available, we immediately saw an opportunity to bring him on board," Breed spokesperson Joe Arellano said at the time of Mo's hiring. "His visibility through KTSF connects with a broad audience, and his professional background and experience made him a strong fit."

Mo is expected to remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings.

"DHS reversed the horrendous Biden-era policy that allowed aliens in our country illegally to jet around our country," The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said about the arrest. "Under President Trump, DHS will no longer tolerate this. This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport."

item.title: Skipping the iPhone 18 Pro? Here's everything you need to make your current phone feel like new
item.description: Skipping the iPhone 18 Pro this year? Refresh your current iPhone with phone cases, screen protectors, MagSafe power banks, chargers and other easy upgrades.
