item.title: Javier Bardem slammed for targeting Pink over Macklemore comments: 'The left is eating itself'
item.description: Actor Javier Bardem promoted a petition to remove Pink as a UNICEF ambassador, drawing fierce pushback from Michael Rapaport and Selma Blair.
item.content:encoded:
Actor Javier Bardem has stepped into the middle of the controversy surrounding Pink, Macklemore and the Israel-Gaza conflict — and is now taking heat for it.

The "No Country for Old Men" star shared multiple posts to his Instagram Stories Monday urging followers to sign a Change.org petition demanding that Pink be removed as a UNICEF ambassador, according to Reuters.

The petition Bardem promoted, titled "Remove Pink as a UNICEF Ambassador," calls on the organization to remove the singer from her position.

ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO

Supporters argue that Pink’s comments are "incompatible with the role of a UNICEF Ambassador" and say ambassadors should promote "peace, understanding, and humanitarian values above personal biases."

The petition urges UNICEF to "take decisive action and remove Pink as an ambassador," arguing that the organization must remain committed to all children regardless of "nationality or heritage."

Bardem’s move drew pushback from fans and fellow celebrities who questioned why the actor was backing an effort to strip Pink of her UNICEF title over comments she made after Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian concert appearance.

Michael Rapaport delivered one of the most blistering responses, mocking Bardem as a "tattletale" and accusing the actor of going after Pink through a petition rather than confronting her directly.

He wrote in an Instagram caption: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb initiated,signed & is promoting a petition to have singer PINK removed as a UNICEF Ambassador. He’s is Bullying a Proud Jewish Woman."

Rapaport continued in his video: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb. Javier Bardem, what the f--- are you doing, you little tattle-tale? Hall monitor … you are a grown man, a grown f---ing man. Pink is a grown woman. You're both world-famous. If you have a problem with what she said, call her. Sit her down, have a coffee, look her dead in the face and express all and any frustrations and questions you have … instead you sign a petition, like a little b---- to have her removed as a UNICEF ambassador. What the f--- is wrong with you?"

PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS

Selma Blair also weighed in in the comment section, writing: "Why would anyone want this great removed from unicef for human , humble and loving words? This makes no sense. I would think the terrifically talented actor man would worry about his own incredible life more. And allow love to flow. And listen to everybody. Not just his echo chamber. But alas."

Bardem's decision to promote the petition also drew criticism from social media users, with commenters questioning why the actor was pushing for Pink's removal over her comments.

One commenter wrote: "I'm not a big Pink fan...I like her music okay, but she was one of the many performers who actually did ads for Big Pharma pushing the vax during covid. That said, who the hell is Bardem to cancel her? The left is eating itself."

Meanwhile, supporters of Bardem's position also commented on the petition.

"Pink chose her and her rich friends' discomfort was more important than people's lives," one commenter wrote, adding that if UNICEF does not "stand with Gaza now and remove Pink," then "the world is a much darker place."

Another argued, "No ambassador can call attention to important issues while actively ignoring and deliberately misunderstanding and misrepresenting the conditions in Palestine. Pink has shown herself incapable of even acknowledging what is clear to the world, and is not fit to serve UNICEF."

A third commenter questioned how Pink could remain a UNICEF advocate while, in their view, failing to support "basic human rights and free speech for all people, especially those in Gaza, the Sudan and the Congo."

Fox News Digital reached out to Bardem, UNICEF and Pink for comment.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT

The petition Bardem promoted centers on Pink’s response to Macklemore’s appearance with Ed Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4.

Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," his song supporting Palestinians, while repeatedly chanting "Free Palestine" as images related to Gaza appeared on a screen behind him.

The performance sparked criticism from the @Stop_Antisemitism Instagram account, which accused Macklemore of using the concert to push "anti-Israel propaganda."

Pink faced backlash after reposting the criticism and subsequently issued her own lengthy explanation.

"I’ve been quiet in my own words for a week, which you know isn’t like me. So here they are," she wrote on social media.

"I was born a Jew," Pink continued. "I didn’t pick it, and I’ve never hidden it."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

She also addressed her position on the conflict.

"Of course I don’t speak for Israel, or for any government. I never have," Pink wrote. "What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organization. Palestinians deserve a future that honors their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody’s child."

Pink also cited her years of work with UNICEF, saying she had spent time with children "on both sides of that fence."

"I’m not going to litigate a complex war in an Instagram caption, and I’m not going to recite anybody’s slogan to earn back a follower," she wrote.

Pink went on to explain that what she was "reacting to" was Macklemore himself. She recalled him performing his song "Same Love" at the Grammys in 2014, and how she cheered on the message, but "Four months later Macklemore put on a hooked nose, a black beard and a bowl cut, performed in it, and called it a 'random costume.'"

"Every Jew I know knew exactly what it was. The same love, it turned out, had a guest list, and we weren’t on it. But he apologized, and I let it go, because that’s what we do. We let it go. Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them."

She added, "You don’t get to decide that for us."

"That’s what prompted my repost," she wrote. "Not 'Free Palestine,' and not anyone’s right to say it. I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I’m not asking now. I don’t need anyone fired, and I don’t need a refund. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, 'that scared me, and it scared people I love,' without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I’m somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?"

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

The controversy surrounding Macklemore's stage appearance continued after the MetLife Stadium performance. Macklemore later posted a video on Instagram addressing the crowd and said performing on Sheeran's tour gave him the opportunity to deliver his "Free Palestine" message to a massive audience.

Macklemore doubled down in the caption and wrote, "Wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial."

He was later dropped from the tour altogether after venues told the tour's promoters that they would "not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup."

item.title: Darren Rovell shows off one his favorite Knicks memorabilia items, which includes notorious Menendez brothers
item.description: Darren Rovell showed off his framed 1990-91 NBA Hoops Mark Jackson card featuring the Menendez brothers sitting courtside after their crimes.
item.content:encoded:
Collecting sports memorabilia can sometimes breed some very interesting results.

One minute, you're looking over a seemingly very mundane trading card in your hand, and the next minute you see a couple of convicted murderers sitting court side in the background.

That's exactly what happened with a 1990-91 NBA Hoops card featuring former New York Knicks point guard and, later, Golden State Warriors head coach Mark Jackson.

A SPORTING GOODS GIANT IS GETTING INTO THE LUCRATIVE, EVER-EXPANDING SPORTS CARD BUSINESS

Jackson's now infamous trading card features a picture from a game between the Los Angeles Clippers and the aforementioned Knicks.

And who is sitting court side in the lower bowl seats? None other than Erik and Lyle Menendez, two brothers who would later be found guilty of the first-degree murder of their parents.

INSIDE 'CELEBRITY ROW' AT NBA PLAYOFFS: QUID PRO QUO DEALS, LOYALTY TESTS AND A-LISTERS WHO GOT BOOTED

The craziest part of this whole story: this picture was taken after the Menendez brothers committed their heinous crimes, allegedly purchasing the seats with money paid out from a life-insurance policy.

Sports business analyst and memorabilia collector Darren Rovell just so happens to be in possession of one of the cards (because of course he does), and he joined OutKick's Craig Carton to share his find.

CRAIG CARTON, MICHAEL RAPAPORT DISH ON THEIR SHARED DISLIKE FOR LEBRON JAMES: 'DEAD TO ME'

"This is one of my favorite Knicks items," Rovell exclaimed as he held up the framed trading card on "The Craig Carton Show." "Read the top of the slab."

As Rovell handed the card over to Carton, the host read aloud.

"Valid: Menendez brothers sit courtside."

Rovell went on to explain the story to Carton, who shockingly wasn't familiar with the lore of the "Mark Jackson/Menendez" card.

"The 1990 Hoops Mark Jackson card has the Menendez brothers sitting courtside," Rovell explained. "What's so crazy is ... they killed their parents before this."

A shocked Carton couldn't believe what he was holding.

"They went to a Knicks game AFTER the murders?"

Both Menendez brothers are currently serving a prison term of 50 years to life, though they are once again appealing for parole after being denied in 2025.

That hearing is set for March 2027.

So, the moral of the story here is a simple one: keep collecting sports memorabilia, kids.

You never know who is going to show up in the background of your favorite player's trading card.

item.title: San Francisco sues Trump Media over alleged 'pay-to-play' Truth Social service
item.description: San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu alleges the paid service gives wealthy subscribers an unfair advantage by providing early access to President Donald Trump's market-moving posts.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's social media company is facing a lawsuit from the city of San Francisco over a paid Truth Social subscription service that gives certain customers early access to the president's posts.

San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu announced the lawsuit Tuesday, alleging that Trump Media's Truth API service operates as a "pay-to-play scheme," allowing subscribers to receive President Donald Trump's market-moving posts before they are publicly available. 

The lawsuit seeks to block the service and impose civil penalties under California's Unfair Competition Law (UCL). 

Chiu alleged the service gives wealthy subscribers an "unfair advantage" by providing early access to government information before it reaches the broader public.

TRUMP WARNS HE'LL BE 'LAST REPUBLICAN PRESIDENT' IF SENATE GOP DOESN'T MAKE MAJOR CHANGE

"Truth Social has knowingly created a marketplace for insider trading by giving high-paying subscribers an unfair advantage over ordinary investors in the market," Chiu said at a news conference Tuesday. "It's a pay-to-play scheme for early access to the president's market-moving government decisions."

The monthly subscription was rolled out Aug. 1 and costs between $60,000 to $100,000 in exchange for early access to market-moving posts from Truth Social accounts with large followings, including Trump’s own account.

"No ordinary person can pay that fee," Chiu said. "Now the early subscribers are largely high-frequency trading firms with the technology to analyze that information and to make trades within microseconds."

TRUMP ANNOUNCES WHITE HOUSE BAN AGAINST THREE MEDIA OUTLETS

Chiu also said Trump owns roughly 41% of Trump Media and "is personally benefiting from this business scheme."

A Trump Media spokesperson pushed back on the allegations, telling Fox News Digital, "The people of California should outsource their future lawsuits to AI chatbots who, unlike the left-wing activists masquerading as attorneys who filed this lawsuit, will grasp the basic distinction between public and nonpublic information."

The lawsuit was filed Monday, the same day that dozens of former federal prosecutors and agents filed a court brief backing a separate lawsuit over Truth API, according to CBS News.

TRUMP’S $100K WALL STREET TRUTH ACCESS DRAWS LAWSUIT; EXPERT WARNS IT ‘RAISES THE STAKES’ ON ETHICS

The separate lawsuit, brought by The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation, alleges the paid service violates the First and Fifth amendments.

A White House spokesperson referred Fox News Digital to Trump Media and The Trump Organization for comment.

Representatives for The Trump Organization and Chiu's office could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

Fox News Digital's Julia Bonavita contributed to this report.

item.title: Russia's neighbor reveals personal appeals to Trump as US weighs NATO troop pullback in Europe
item.description: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda revealed he sent two letters to Trump urging U.S. troops to stay on NATO's eastern flank amid Russian threat.
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK — Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda revealed Monday he personally pleaded with President Donald Trump to maintain U.S. forces on NATO’s eastern flank as Washington reviews its military footprint in Europe.

Meanwhile, Russia’s war in Ukraine has raged on for more than 4½ years and raised questions about how far Moscow will push into the continent.

Nausėda said during remarks at a fireside chat moderated by Fox News Digital at the Presidential Business Forum on Resilience on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly New York that Lithuania is prepared to provide "very generous host nation support" for American forces to remain in the region.

"I personally sent two letters to the president," Nausėda said of the plea to keep an American troops' presence.

PENTAGON CUTS BRIGADE COMBAT TEAMS IN EUROPE AS TRUMP PRESSURES NATO ON SPENDING

The Pentagon has already begun scaling back some forces and capabilities in Europe, while reported options under review could remove tens of thousands more troops.

The review is part of a broader Pentagon strategy to shift primary responsibility for Europe’s conventional defense onto European allies, while reserving a more limited U.S. role. But Washington has also signaled that its retrenchment may not be uniform: Trump said last week that the U.S. was making progress toward a permanent Army base in Poland, one of NATO’s highest-spending members.

That has left frontline allies trying to determine where they fit in with an emerging U.S. strategy that calls for a smaller overall role in Europe while deepening ties with countries Washington views as carrying more of the burden.

The review also comes as Russia’s war with Ukraine has increasingly spilled into NATO territory.

RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS

Lithuania experienced that threat firsthand last week when NATO fighters shot down a drone that crossed into Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. Nausėda later said the aircraft was likely Russian and intended for an attack on Ukraine before veering off course.

The country's intelligence services warn that Russia is already rebuilding military capabilities near NATO's eastern borders despite its losses in Ukraine.

Lithuania's 2026 National Threat Assessment found that a ceasefire or frozen conflict in Ukraine could accelerate that buildup, allowing Moscow to move more troops and equipment back toward permanent bases near the Baltic States and replenish weapons and ammunition depleted during the war. 

In that scenario, Lithuanian intelligence assessed Russia could eventually develop enough capability to launch military action against the Baltics and seek an initial regional advantage before NATO could fully respond.

Asked how much time NATO would have if a ceasefire were reached tomorrow, Nausėda declined to put a timeline on the threat but warned that "a ceasefire for Russia may mean" looking for new targets.

He said whether Moscow ultimately tests NATO would depend largely on the alliance's ability to strengthen its deterrence and demonstrate that it can defend its eastern flank.

Nausėda cast doubt on the prospect of near-term peace talks, saying that "for the time being, Russia is not ready to start the peace negotiations."

Instead, he said Moscow appears intent on using the approaching winter to increase pressure on Kyiv by striking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and worsening conditions for civilians.

"The winter is coming. Russia knows very well where they should target, and they will target energy infrastructure first of all," Nausėda said, describing the attacks as an effort to make living conditions in Ukraine as difficult as possible and pressure its leadership toward concessions.

"For these negotiations, I don’t see any ground, at least right now," he said, adding that talks could become possible "maybe next year."

The threat to energy infrastructure was particularly resonant for Nausėda, who spoke as Lithuania marked another step in its yearslong effort to insulate itself from energy pressure from Moscow.

Lithuania, marking a new long-term natural gas agreement with U.S. natural gas producer EQT Corp. this week during the president's trip to New York, began importing U.S. LNG in 2017 and now gets roughly 70% of its LNG from the United States, Nausėda said.

During Monday’s forum, Lithuanian energy company Ignitis signed a new long-term LNG agreement with U.S.-based EQT Corp.

Nausėda said Lithuania’s push for energy independence was shaped by years of experience with Moscow using the country’s dependence on Russian energy as political leverage.

"Our history shows that, all the time, Russians misused our dependencies for their own benefit," Nausėda said.

Nausėda stressed that Lithuania is also increasing its own defense burden, saying the country is spending 5.4% of GDP on defense while building a national division and preparing to host a full German brigade by the end of 2027.

He said Lithuanian intelligence has periodically warned of a risk that Russia could target critical infrastructure in Lithuania, prompting additional measures to protect energy and other strategic assets.

item.title: Why didn't Ryan Clark push back at Colin Kaepernick comparing the NFL to slavery during interview?
item.description: Colin Kaepernick doubled down on his NFL-slave trade comparison in a podcast interview with Ryan Clark, calling the NFL Combine a "meat market."
item.content:encoded:
Colin Kaepernick doubled down on his comparison of the NFL to the slave trade during a podcast interview with former ESPN commentator Ryan Clark this week.

"When did you truly start to have the realization that [the combine] reminds [you] of the slave trade?" Clark asked.

"You get to the point, where it's like, 'Strip down to your drawers,’" Kaepernick responded. "It feels like a meat market."

5 TOUGH QUESTIONS COLIN KAEPERNICK DIDN'T HEAR DURING HIS MEDIA TOUR | MATT CALKINS

Kaepernick added that he did not have the "historical perspective at the time" in 2011 at the Scouting Combine to understand what he now considers a "parallel" to a slave auction.

The former NFL quarterback first made the comparison during a 2021 Netflix series. His reputation has never been the same since. That is how offensive it is to equate the horrors of bondage with playing in the NFL for millions of dollars a year.

But at this point, similar scrutiny must be applied to Clark.

Consider the wording of Clark's question. He did not challenge Kaepernick's premise or ask him to substantiate it. Instead, he led him toward the desired answer by asking "when" he realized the NFL draft process resembled slavery.

COLIN KAEPERNICK IS STILL UPSET THAT HIS MOM WANTED HIM TO DATE TAYLOR SWIFT, A WHITE WOMAN

Clark then nodded along as Kaepernick claimed that the draft and slave auctions are part of the "same process."

OutKick asked Clark on Tuesday about his question to Kaepernick. We also asked whether he agreed with the analogy. Clark did not respond by the time of publication. We will update this story if he does.

At minimum, it is reasonable to conclude that Clark did not find the comparison outrageous. We have seen how he reacts when he disagrees with a statement. Just ask ESPN host Peter Schrager, whom Clark continued to shout at behind the scenes after an on-air disagreement last year.

On the merits, Kaepernick's analogy is indefensible. No serious person could reasonably equate the NFL draft process with an auction block.

As the interviewer, Clark had a responsibility to identify the absurdity of the claim. He owed that to his audience. He did not live up to that responsibility.

RYAN CLARK AGAIN ACCUSES ESPN OF LEAKING HIS FIRING TO OUTKICK: HERE’S THE REAL STORY

By allowing Kaepernick to promote such baseless hysteria, Clark turned his platform into an infomercial for the former quarterback's propaganda campaign.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And Clark knows better. He participated in the very process Kaepernick characterized as exploitative. Clark played 13 seasons in the NFL, a career he claims to revere.

There is virtually no chance Clark saw his time in the league as comparable to servitude.

That is what makes conversations like this sound dishonest and contrived. Kaepernick and Clark come across as two entitled millionaires attempting to convince average Americans that they are the true victims of American society.

It is deeply distasteful.

Still, we hope Clark responds. We'd like to put on the record his official reaction to Kaepernick comparing the NFL to the slave trade.
